messages:
Maya: quick question — can we settle who "owns" streaming request lifecycle for retries/resume? e.g. client→gateway→upstream. Trying to avoid ambiguous handoffs during midstream failures.
Luca: short answer: need explicit ownership model. either gateway acts as fabric (sticky) and stores resume tokens, or upstream is authoritative and returns tokens in trailers. mixing both gets messy.
Elena: +1. also we should be explicit about what gateway is allowed to retry vs when it must surface error to client. idempotency + side-effect safety are still the core constraints.
Sanjay: ops perspective: if gateway stores tokens for resume, that's memory + billing churn. we should cap per-tenant tokens and TTL like 30s-5m depending on model.
Maya: thinking about tradeoffs: gateway-stored tokens = fast failover and no client changes. upstream-issued tokens = simpler gateway but requires upstream changes and client awareness.
Luca: gateway-stored token flow (sketch):
1) client starts streaming request -> gateway forwards to upstream
2) upstream returns partial responses (streaming) and optionally trailers with resume token
3) gateway caches token keyed by request-id + tenant, expires after TTL
4) on upstream disconnect, gateway can attempt a resume by re-attaching to upstream using cached token (if policy allows)
This lets gateway do transparent retries for low-latency cases.
Elena: downside: gateway needs to know how to attach resume token to upstream protocol. that's an interface contract. we should standardize a header/trailer pair.
Proposal headers/trailers (draft):
Request headers:
X-Request-Id: <uuid>
X-Stream-Owner: edge|upstream
Idempotency-Key: <sha256>
Trailers (from upstream):
X-Resume-Token: <opaque>
X-Resume-Last-Offset: <int>
If X-Stream-Owner=edge, gateway may replay/resume. If upstream, gateway must surface the token to client.
Example (pseudo):
POST /v1/generate/stream
Headers:
  X-Request-Id: 3f2a...
  X-Stream-Owner: upstream
  Content-Type: application/json
--stream chunks--
(trailer) X-Resume-Token: zYx123
Sanjay: note: trailers are not available in HTTP/1.1 chunked responses for browsers easily. if clients are browsers, we need a JSON in final chunk as fallback with resume info.
Maya: good catch. so spec should cover three modes: http/2+ trailers, http/1.1 chunk final message containing resume metadata, and explicit websocket/RTC control channel.
Luca: also need to handle backpressure signals. gateway should not drop client-sent flow-control frames. propose we preserve upstream backpressure semantics and surface them to client where possible.
Elena: one more policy: when retrying midstream, gateway must ensure no duplicate side-effects. so require Idempotency-Key + server-side check. if not provided, only safe read-only retries.
Sanjay: infra constraint: cache keys must include model-id + tenant + request-id to avoid token reuse across models or tenants.
Maya: question for API owners: if upgrade to "gateway-owned" resume is permitted, do we want it on by default or opt-in per route? my vote: opt-in per route with opt-out when customers demand explicit tokens.
Elena: opt-in seems safer. default to upstream-owned so no silent resource use by gateway. customers can enable gateway-resume for low-latency UX.
Luca: we should also add observability hooks: counts of resume attempts, cache hits/misses, resume latency, and cases where resume failed due to idempotency mismatch.
Maya: agree. also add an SLA note: transparent gateway resume should have a bounded retry budget (e.g., max 2 resume attempts within 30s).
Sanjay: ops-bot reminder: please include per-tenant quotas for resume tokens and a cleanup job for expired tokens to avoid memory leak.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: FYI canary of gateway/v25 with streaming-trailers enabled passed smoke tests in us-west-2 :white_check_mark:
Elena: next steps for RFC follow-up:
- finalize header/trailer names and fallback JSON schema (Elena)
- add per-route opt-in flag + default behavior (Maya)
- implement cache TTL + quota plan (Sanjay)
- add observability metrics and resume audit log (Luca)
Maya: thanks — assigning owners above. will sync in next architecture sync. :thumbsup:
